source.quote: One Call API, endpoint version 3.0, remains available today and isn't being switched off as part of this release.

tasks.reasoning:
The repo calls the legacy One Call 2.5 endpoint (/data/2.5/onecall), which is older than both versions in this change. OpenWeatherMap has publicly retired One Call 2.5 in favour of 3.0. This notice keeps 3.0 available but recommends 4.0, so the endpoint the repo calls is not the one being kept, and the call at line 47 is likely already failing or about to fail. The natural fix is to migrate straight to 4.0. That migration means:
- calling /current and /timeline/1h and /timeline/1day instead of one combined call;
- reading values under `data`;
- following next/prev pagination, with each page billed;
- fetching alerts by ID, if alerts are displayed.

Uncertain: the notice does not mention 2.5, and the scan did not read how the stored Forecast JSON is consumed. The migration agent should:
- check whether the 2.5 call still returns 200 with the current key;
- find every template or model that reads current/hourly/daily/alerts from Forecast rows;
- decide whether 3.0 is a lower-effort interim target. 3.0 keeps the combined response shape, but 4.0 is the recommended version.

Rated high because the forecast feature is likely already broken on the retired 2.5 endpoint.
This task also resolves these changes. Handle each in the same change, and say in the PR how:
- openweathermap:one-call-4-split-endpoints-exclude (endpoint-removed): One Call 4.0 replaces the combined 3.0 response (and exclude param) with separate endpoints; /timemachine is folded into the hourly timeline (migration is optional, unsure of 3.0 retirement). 4.0 replaces the single combined One Call response with separate /current and /timeline/* endpoints. A move from 2.5 to 4.0 means rewriting the single GET in weather/views.py as several calls. That rewrite is part of this migration and needs no separate PR.
  Source: https://openweathermap.org/api/one-call-3-migration.md
  "For that particular case, please use the Hourly endpoint in the One Call API, endpoint version 4.0 (`/timeline/1h`) instead of the Time machine endpoint in the One Call API, endpoint version 3.0 (`/timemachine`)."
- openweathermap:one-call-4-response-paths-alerts (field-renamed): One Call 4.0 response fields move under `data` (e.g. current.temp -> data.temp); alerts become IDs needing a second call to /onecall/alert/{alert_id}; daily.summary and alerts.tags are dropped. In 4.0, fields move under `data` and alerts become IDs fetched from /onecall/alert/{alert_id}. This only matters once the code calls 4.0. Code that reads the stored Forecast JSON (current/hourly/daily) must be updated as part of the same migration.
  Source: https://openweathermap.org/api/one-call-3-migration.md
  "For that particular case, please use the Weather alerts endpoint in One Call API, endpoint version 4.0 (`/onecall/alert/{alert_id}`), instead of the Current & Forecasts endpoint in One Call API, endpoint version 3.0 (inline `alerts[]`)."
- openweathermap:one-call-4-pagination-billing (pagination-or-limits): One Call 4.0 paginates large timeline responses via next/prev links, and each page is billed as a separate call. Pagination via next/prev, with each page billed separately, only applies to 4.0 timeline endpoints. The migration must handle following next links, or limit the requested range to control cost, as part of the same edit.
  Source: https://openweathermap.org/api/one-call-3-migration.md
  "| Paginated requests | Not applicable | Each `next`/`prev` page is billed as its own call |"

callSites.why: Calls GET /data/2.5/onecall (lat, lon, appid), asserts 200 and stores the combined JSON as Forecast rows. 4.0 splits this into /data/4.0/onecall/current plus /timeline/1h and /timeline/1day, with fields nested under `data`.
The pinned base path data/2.5 must change to data/4.0/onecall/*.

record.prBody:
## One Call API 4.0 (/data/4.0/onecall/*) launched as new modular endpoint version; 3.0 stays available but 4.0 recommended for new integrations [Needs review]

### Change

The weather fetch in weather/views.py now calls One Call 4.0 `/data/4.0/onecall/timeline/1day` instead of the retired `/data/2.5/onecall`. Same lat, lon and appid params. `Forecast.create_all_from_json` reads day records from `data` (4.0) and falls back to `daily` (legacy shape). Stored per-day JSON keeps the same field names, so shift.html (weather, wind_speed, wind_gust, uvi, humidity) is unchanged. I updated the existing test's URL and added a new DB-free test, weather/test_one_call_4.py.

How the three bundled changes were handled:
- **Split endpoints / `exclude`:** the app only stores daily records, so only `/timeline/1day` is called. `/current`, `/timeline/1h` and `/timemachine` are not used.
- **Response paths and alerts:** records are read under `data`. The app never reads alerts, so no `/onecall/alert/{id}` calls are made. `daily.summary` and `alerts.tags` are not read anywhere in the repo.
- **Pagination billing:** `/timeline/1day` returns up to 10 days per page, which covers the 8 days 2.5 gave. Only the first page is fetched and `next`/`prev` are not followed, so there is one billed call per refresh.

Files touched:
- `pillarpointstewards/weather/models.py`
- `pillarpointstewards/weather/test_one_call_4.py`
- `pillarpointstewards/weather/tests.py`
- `pillarpointstewards/weather/views.py`

### Why

The repo called One Call 2.5, which is older than both 3.0 and 4.0 and has been retired. 4.0 is the recommended version. It replaces the combined response with separate endpoints and puts records under `data`, so both the request URL and the code that reads the stored response had to change.

> One Call API, endpoint version 3.0, remains available today and isn't being switched off as part of this release.

Source: https://openweathermap.org/api/one-call-3-migration.md

### Proof

| Check | Before | After | New failures |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| weather-tests | fail (2) | fail (4) | 2 |
| one-call-4-proof | fail (1) | pass | 0 |

New failures: 2

Checks added by the agent (they count toward proof; check that each command really tests the change):
- weather-tests, added by the agent: `cd pillarpointstewards && python -m pytest weather/tests.py -q` (fail (2) → fail (4))
- one-call-4-proof, added by the agent: `cd pillarpointstewards && python -m pytest weather/test_one_call_4.py -q` (fail (1) → pass)

Provider tool calls recorded by the harness:
- `openweathermap__openapi_check`: fail

The agent's validator claims (not proof; graded against the recorded calls):
- openweathermap__openapi_check: fail (Could not run: the docs URL is not an OpenAPI spec, so nothing was validated. I checked the request against the 4.0 docs by hand.)

Test of this change: `one-call-4-proof`, written by the agent and run with the checks.

Where checks ran: Docker container python:3.12-bookworm; install scripts disabled; no host env or mounts besides the repo copy; no credentials, so no live API calls

### Unproven

- Live 4.0 response shape was not seen. I relied on the docs example.
- The existing DB-backed weather/tests.py could not run here. The sandbox has no Postgres, and sqlite fails on the dashboard connection's options. I changed its URL assertion by hand and added a 4.0 DB-backed test (test_post_to_update_weather_one_call_4) that has not been run.
- The API key needs the 'One Call API' subscription that 4.0 requires.
- The openapi_check validator could not run because no OpenAPI spec URL was available.
- weather-tests: new failure `FAILED weather/tests.py::test_post_to_update_weather_one_call_4`
- weather-tests: new failure `ERROR weather/tests.py::test_post_to_update_weather_one_call_4`
- weather-tests was already failing before the change and still fails.
- Validator openweathermap__openapi_check failed: openapi_check failed to run: https://openweathermap.org/api/one-call-4: could not parse it as JSON or YAML (unexpected ":" (a mapping is not allowed here; check the indentation) (line 3, column 9527))

### Behaviour changes

- Each refresh now fetches up to 10 daily records instead of 8, so up to 10 Forecast rows are stored per location instead of 8.
- The 4.0 daily records have no `summary`. Nothing in the repo reads it.
- Units are unchanged (standard/Kelvin, as before), because no `units` param is sent.
- Only the first page of the 1day timeline is fetched, so there is no extra billing for `next`/`prev`.
- The daily endpoint's record window may start from the current day rather than exactly where 2.5's daily array started. A live call would confirm this.

---

review.summary: The diff moves the single call site (views.py:39) from the old /data/2.5/onecall to /data/4.0/onecall/timeline/1day. models.py accepts either `data` or `daily`. The cited change does not force this move: it says 3.0 stays available. 2.5 is the legacy path, so moving off it is reasonable, but the PR jumps to a new modular endpoint whose response shape is only assumed. The tests mock it with a copy of the 2.5 `daily` records. Nothing confirms that 4.0 returns top-level `lat`/`lon`, or per-day records with `dt`, `temp.day`, `weather` and `wind_speed` in the same units. Those records are stored verbatim in `Forecast.details` and read downstream. weather-tests got worse (2 → 4 failures) and the PR does not explain why. The only passing check is a fully mocked proof. needs-review is the right grade.

concerns.issue: Lines 47-56 assume the 4.0 /timeline/1day response has top-level `lat`/`lon` and that each record under `data` has `dt` as UTC midnight, which `create_from_json` relies on for the date. I could not confirm any of this from the quoted source. If the 4.0 response nests coordinates or names the timestamp differently, this raises KeyError or stores the wrong dates. Check the 4.0 timeline docs or a real response.

Each record is stored as-is in `Forecast.details`, and GET /fetch-weather/?include_forecasts returns it to consumers. If 4.0 day records differ from 2.5 `daily` records (field names, nesting, or default units: 2.5 defaulted to Kelvin, as the fixtures show), downstream display changes without warning. Nothing in the PR checks this.

weather-tests went from 2 failures before to 4 after. The PR does not say whether the two extra failures are the new DB tests failing for the same environmental reason or real regressions. Also, `test_post_to_update_weather_one_call_4` only rewraps the 2.5 `daily` fixture under `data`, and `{**record, "dt": record["dt"]}` is a no-op. It proves the fallback branch works, not compatibility with 4.0.
The one-call-4-proof check mocks httpx, Location and Forecast. It only proves that the URL string changed. No live call or recorded 4.0 response was exercised.

The PR switches the endpoint without confirming that the existing API key or subscription is entitled to 4.0. The view still uses `assert response.status_code == 200`, so a 401/403 from a plan mismatch would surface as an unhandled 500.
The comment says the first page holds up to 10 days and that following `next` is billed. I could not confirm this from the quoted source. Verify it against the 4.0 docs, or drop the comment.

Find out why weather-tests went from 2 to 4 failures. Run it with a working DB and check whether test_post_to_update_weather and the new test pass.
